desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

name: Eldritch Master
desc:
At 20th level, you can draw on your inner reserve of mystical power while entreating your patron to regain expended spell slots. You can spend 1 minute entreating your patron for aid to regain all your expended spell slots from your Pact Magic feature.
Once you regain spell slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

name: Spellcasting: Wizard
desc: As a student of arcane magic, you have a spellbook containing spells that show the first glimmerings of your true power.

name: Arcane Recovery
desc:
You have learned to regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your wizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.
For example, if you're a 4th-level wizard, you can recover up to two levels worth of spell slots. You can recover either a 2nd-level spell slot or two 1st-level spell slots.

name: Arcane Tradition
desc:
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

name: Evocation Savant
desc: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the gold and time you must spend to copy an evocation spell into your spellbook is halved.

name: Sculpt Spells
desc: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocation spells. When you cast an evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

name: Arcane Tradition feature
desc:
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

name: Potent Cantrip
desc: Starting at 6th level, your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your cantrip, the creature takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

name: Arcane Tradition feature
desc:
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

name: Empowered Evocation
desc: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to one damage roll of any wizard evocation spell you cast.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

name: Arcane Tradition feature
desc:
When you reach 2nd level, you choose an arcane tradition, shaping your practice of magic through one of eight schools, such as Evocation.
Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

name: Overchannel
desc:
Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler spells. When you cast a wizard spell of 1st through 5th level that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a long rest, you take 2d12 necrotic damage for each level of the spell, immediately after you cast it. Each time you use this feature again before finishing a long rest, the necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12. This damage ignores resistance and immunity.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

name: Spell Mastery
desc:
At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level wizard spell and a 2nd-level wizard spell that are in your spellbook. You can cast those spells at their lowest level without expending a spell slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.
By spending 8 hours in study, you can exchange one or both of the spells you chose for different spells of the same levels.

name: Ability Score Improvement
desc: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

name: Signature Spell
desc:
When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful spells and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level wizard spells in your spellbook as your signature spells. You always have these spells prepared, they don't count against the number of spells you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a spell slot. When you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest.
If you want to cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot as normal.

name: Spirit Seeker
desc: You can cast beast sense and speak with animals, but only as rituals: each takes 10 minutes longer than its normal casting time and needs no spell slot. Beast sense lets you touch a willing beast and share its sight and hearing for up to 1 hour (concentration), during which you are blind and deaf to your own surroundings. Speak with animals lets you understand and talk with beasts for 10 minutes. You don't otherwise know or prepare these spells.

name: Totem Spirit
desc: Pick a totem animal and gain the benefit below. You also make or find a physical totem (an amulet, charm or similar token) that includes a piece of that animal, such as fur, a feather, a claw or a tooth, and you may pick up small physical traits that recall it.

name: Totem Spirit: Bear
desc: While raging, you have resistance to every damage type except psychic.

name: Totem Spirit: Eagle
desc: While raging and not wearing heavy armor, opportunity attacks against you are made with disadvantage, and you can take the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn.

name: Totem Spirit: Wolf
desc: While you are raging, your allies have advantage on melee attack rolls against any creature hostile to you that is within 5 feet of you.

name: Aspect of the Beast
desc: Pick a totem animal, the same one you chose before or a different one, and gain the benefit below. These benefits work all the time, not only while raging.

name: Aspect of the Beast: Bear
desc: Your carrying capacity, including the most you can push, drag or lift, is doubled, and you have advantage on Strength checks to push, pull, lift or break objects.

name: Aspect of the Beast: Eagle
desc: You see clearly out to 1 mile, making out fine details as if they were no more than 100 feet away. Dim light doesn't give you disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks.

name: Aspect of the Beast: Wolf
desc: You can track creatures while traveling at a fast pace, and you can move stealthily while traveling at a normal pace (normally stealth needs a slow pace).

name: Spirit Walker
desc: You can cast commune with nature, but only as a ritual (10 minutes longer than its 1-minute casting time, no spell slot). It tells you up to three facts about the land within 3 miles of you (300 feet underground), such as terrain, water, plants, animals, people, powerful creatures or the influence of other planes. The answers are delivered by a spirit form of one of the animals you chose for Totem Spirit or Aspect of the Beast.

name: Totemic Attunement
desc: Pick a totem animal, whichever you chose before, and gain the benefit below.

name: Totemic Attunement: Bear
desc: While you are raging, each hostile creature within 5 feet of you has disadvantage on attack rolls against any target other than you or another creature with this feature. A creature is unaffected if it can't see or hear you or can't be frightened.

name: Totemic Attunement: Eagle
desc: While raging, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed. You can only fly in short bursts: if you end your turn in the air with nothing else holding you up, you fall.

name: Totemic Attunement: Wolf
desc: While raging, when you hit a Large or smaller creature with a melee weapon attack, you can use a bonus action on your turn to knock it prone.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
desc: You become proficient with medium armor, shields and martial weapons.

name: Combat Inspiration
desc: A creature holding one of your Bardic Inspiration dice can also spend it in combat. Right after rolling damage for a weapon attack, it can roll the die and add the result to that damage. Or, when an attack roll is made against it, it can use its reaction to roll the die and add the result to its AC against that one attack, deciding after the attack is rolled but before knowing whether it hits.

name: Extra Attack
desc: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you make two attacks instead of one.

name: Battle Magic
desc: When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

name: Blessings of Knowledge: Languages
desc: You learn two languages of your choice.

name: Blessings of Knowledge: Skills
desc: Choose two of Arcana, History, Nature and Religion. You become proficient in both, and your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with either of them.

name: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity and choose one skill or tool. You are proficient with it for the next 10 minutes.

name: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity and choose a creature you can see within 60 feet. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a success, you can't use this feature on it again until you finish a long rest. On a failure, for 1 minute you can read its surface thoughts (its current feelings and what it is actively thinking about) while it is within 60 feet of you. During that minute you can use your action to end the effect and cast suggestion on the creature without expending a spell slot; it automatically fails its saving throw against that suggestion.

name: Potent Spellcasting
desc: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

name: Visions of the Past
desc:
You can meditate and pray for at least 1 minute to see hazy, dreamlike visions of recent events tied to an object you hold or to the place around you. You can keep meditating for up to a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score, concentrating as if on a spell. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Object reading: holding an object, after 1 minute you learn how its previous owner came to have it and lost it, and the most recent significant event involving the object and that owner. If other creatures owned it within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score, each extra minute reveals the same for one more of those owners.
Area reading: you see recent events in your immediate surroundings (a room, street, tunnel, clearing or similar space, up to a 50-foot cube), going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score. Each minute of meditation reveals one significant event, most recent first: usually an emotionally charged moment such as violence, treachery, a celebration or a death, or an everyday happening that matters to your current situation.

name: Bonus Cantrip
desc: You learn the light cantrip if you don't already know it. It doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

name: Warding Flare
desc: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you attacks you, you can use your reaction to flash bright light in its eyes before the attack hits or misses, giving the attack roll disadvantage. Creatures that can't be blinded are immune. You can use this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity and present your holy symbol. All magical darkness within 30 feet of you is dispelled, and each hostile creature within 30 feet makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 2d10 + your cleric level radiant damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. Creatures with total cover from you are unaffected.

name: Improved Flare
desc: You can also use Warding Flare when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

name: Potent Spellcasting
desc: Add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

name: Corona of Light
desc: As an action, wrap yourself in an aura of sunlight for 1 minute, or until you end it with another action. You shed bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light for another 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any spell that deals fire or radiant damage.

name: Acolyte of Nature: Cantrip
desc: You learn one cantrip of your choice from the druid spell list, on top of your usual cantrips. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

name: Acolyte of Nature: Skill
desc: You become proficient in one of these skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature or Survival.

name: Bonus Proficiency
desc: You become proficient with heavy armor.

name: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity, present your holy symbol and call on your deity. Each beast or plant creature within 30 feet of you that can see you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage, and while charmed it is friendly to you and to any creatures you name.

name: Dampen Elements
desc: When you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to give that creature resistance to that instance of the damage.

name: Divine Strike
desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire or lightning damage (your choice) to it. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

name: Master of Nature
desc: While creatures are charmed by your Charm Animals and Plants, you can use a bonus action on your turn to tell each of them aloud what it will do on its next turn.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
desc: You become proficient with martial weapons and heavy armor.

name: Wrath of the Storm
desc: When a creature you can see within 5 feet of you hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to make it attempt a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. It takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failure, or half as much on a success. You can use this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
desc: When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can spend one use of Channel Divinity to deal the maximum possible damage instead of rolling.

name: Thunderbolt Strike
desc: When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

name: Divine Strike
desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage to it. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

name: Stormborn
desc: Whenever you are not underground or indoors, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed.

name: Blessing of the Trickster
desc: As an action, touch a willing creature other than yourself. It has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks for 1 hour, or until you use this feature again.

name: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity to create a flawless illusion of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. It lasts 1 minute, or until you lose concentration (as if concentrating on a spell). As a bonus action on your turn, you can move it up to 30 feet to a space you can see, but it must stay within 120 feet of you. While it lasts, you can cast spells as though you were in the illusion's space, but you still use your own senses. When both you and the illusion are within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

name: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
desc: As an action, spend one use of Channel Divinity to become invisible until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a spell.

name: Divine Strike
desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to it. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

name: Improved Duplicity
desc: Invoke Duplicity now creates up to four illusions of you instead of one. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any number of them up to 30 feet each, keeping them within 120 feet of you.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
desc: You become proficient with martial weapons and heavy armor.

name: War Priest
desc: When you take the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1) and regain all uses when you finish a long rest.

name: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
desc: When you make an attack roll, you can spend one use of Channel Divinity to add +10 to it. You decide after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

name: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
desc: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction and one use of Channel Divinity to give it +10 on that roll. You decide after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

name: Divine Strike
desc: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type the weapon deals. At 14th level the extra damage becomes 2d8.

name: Avatar of Battle
desc: You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

name: Combat Wild Shape
desc: You can use Wild Shape as a bonus action instead of an action. While transformed by Wild Shape, you can use a bonus action to expend a spell slot and regain 1d8 hit points per level of the slot spent.

name: Circle Forms
desc: Your Wild Shape can turn you into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1, ignoring the Max. CR column of the Beast Shapes table. Its other limits still apply: no swimming speed before 4th level and no flying speed before 8th. From 6th level, the highest challenge rating you can take is your druid level divided by 3, rounded down.

name: Primal Strike
desc: Your attacks in beast form count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

name: Elemental Wild Shape
desc: You can spend two uses of Wild Shape at once to transform into an air elemental, earth elemental, fire elemental or water elemental.

name: Thousand Forms
desc: You can cast alter self at will, without expending a spell slot.

name: Combat Superiority
desc: You learn three maneuvers of your choice and gain four superiority dice, which are d8s. Using a maneuver spends one superiority die, with no more than one maneuver per attack. You regain all spent superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest. You gain a fifth die at 7th level and a sixth at 15th, and you learn two more maneuvers at 7th, 10th and 15th level; whenever you learn new maneuvers you may also swap one maneuver you know for a different one. When a maneuver calls for a saving throw, the DC is your maneuver save DC: 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

name: Maneuver: Commander's Strike
desc: When you take the Attack action, give up one of your attacks and use your bonus action to spend a superiority die. A friendly creature that can see or hear you may immediately use its reaction to make one weapon attack, adding the die to its damage roll.

name: Maneuver: Disarming Attack
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The target makes a Strength save against your maneuver save DC; on a failure it drops one item of your choice that it is holding, which lands at its feet.

name: Maneuver: Distracting Strike
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The next attack roll against that target by anyone other than you has advantage, as long as it is made before the start of your next turn.

name: Maneuver: Evasive Footwork
desc: As you move, you can spend a superiority die: roll it and add the result to your AC for the rest of that movement.

name: Maneuver: Feinting Attack
desc: As a bonus action on your turn, spend a superiority die to feint at one creature within 5 feet of you. You have advantage on your next attack roll against it this turn, and if that attack hits, add the die to the damage.

name: Maneuver: Goading Attack
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The target makes a Wisdom save against your maneuver save DC; on a failure it has disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone other than you until the end of your next turn.

name: Maneuver: Lunging Attack
desc: When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, spend a superiority die to give that attack 5 extra feet of reach. On a hit, add the die to the damage.

name: Maneuver: Maneuvering Attack
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. Choose a friendly creature that can see or hear you: it can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks from your target.

name: Maneuver: Menacing Attack
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. The target makes a Wisdom save against your maneuver save DC or is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

name: Maneuver: Parry
desc: If a creature's melee attack deals you damage, you can react by spending a superiority die: the damage drops by the die roll + your Dexterity modifier.

name: Maneuver: Precision Attack
desc: When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, spend a superiority die and add it to the attack roll. You can decide before or after rolling, but before the attack's effects are applied.

name: Maneuver: Pushing Attack
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it makes a Strength save against your maneuver save DC or is pushed up to 15 feet away from you.

name: Maneuver: Rally
desc: On your turn, use a bonus action and spend a superiority die. A friendly creature that can see or hear you gains temporary hit points equal to the die roll + your Charisma modifier.

name: Maneuver: Riposte
desc: If a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can react by spending a superiority die to strike back with a melee weapon attack; on a hit, the die is added to the damage.

name: Maneuver: Sweeping Attack
desc: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, spend a superiority die to carry the blow into a second creature within 5 feet of the first and within your reach. If your original attack roll would also hit the second creature, it takes damage equal to the die roll, of the same type as the original attack.

name: Maneuver: Trip Attack
desc: On a hit with a weapon attack, spend a superiority die and add it to the damage. If the target is Large or smaller, it makes a Strength save against your maneuver save DC or is knocked prone.

name: Student of War
desc: Pick one type of artisan's tools: you are now proficient with it.

name: Know Your Enemy
desc: If you spend at least 1 minute watching or dealing with a creature outside combat, you can size it up against yourself. Pick two of the following and the DM tells you whether the creature is your equal, your superior or your inferior in each: Strength score, Dexterity score, Constitution score, Armor Class, current hit points, total class levels (if any), or fighter levels (if any).

name: Additional Maneuvers
desc: You learn two more maneuvers of your choice, and you may swap one maneuver you already know for a different one. You also gain a fifth superiority die.

name: Improved Combat Superiority
desc: Your superiority dice become d10s. At 18th level they become d12s.

name: Additional Maneuvers
desc: You learn two more maneuvers of your choice, and you may swap one maneuver you already know for a different one.

name: Relentless
desc: If you have no superiority dice left when you roll initiative, one die comes back to you.

name: Additional Maneuvers
desc: You learn two more maneuvers of your choice, and you may swap one maneuver you already know for a different one. You also gain a sixth superiority die.

name: Improved Combat Superiority (d12)
desc: Your superiority dice become d12s.

name: Spellcasting
desc: You learn wizard spells and cast them with Intelligence: your spell save DC is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier, and your spell attack modifier is your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier. You know two wizard cantrips of your choice, and a third at 10th level. At 3rd level you know three 1st-level wizard spells, two of which must be abjuration or evocation. Every spell you learn later must also be abjuration or evocation, except the ones you learn at 8th, 14th and 20th level, which can come from any school; each must be of a level you have spell slots for (your slots follow the Eldritch Knight third-caster table, reaching 4th-level spells at 19th level). You don't prepare spells: you cast the ones you know. Whenever you gain a fighter level, you may replace one wizard spell you know with another of a level you have slots for, which must be abjuration or evocation unless it replaces one of your any-school spells.

name: Weapon Bond
desc: Through a 1-hour ritual (which you can perform during a short rest), with the weapon within your reach the whole time, you bond yourself to a weapon you touch. While bonded, you can't be disarmed of it unless you are incapacitated, and if it is on the same plane of existence as you, you can use a bonus action on your turn to make it teleport instantly into your hand. You can have up to two bonded weapons but summon only one per bonus action; to bond a third, you must first break the bond with one of the other two.

name: War Magic
desc: Casting a cantrip with your action lets you make one weapon attack as a bonus action that turn.

name: Eldritch Strike
desc: A creature you hit with a weapon attack is left open to your magic: until the end of your next turn, it makes its next saving throw against one of your spells with disadvantage.

name: Arcane Charge
desc: When you use Action Surge, you can also teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, either before or after the extra action.

name: Improved War Magic
desc: Casting any spell with your action, cantrip or leveled, lets you make one weapon attack as a bonus action that turn.

name: Shadow Arts
desc: As an action, you can spend 2 ki points to cast darkness, darkvision, pass without trace or silence, without needing material components. These spells otherwise follow their normal rules, including concentration. You also know the minor illusion cantrip (nothing changes if you already knew it).

name: Shadow Step
desc: As a bonus action while you stand in dim light or darkness, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also dimly lit or dark. Your first melee attack before the turn ends has advantage.

name: Cloak of Shadows
desc: In dim light or darkness, you can spend your action to turn invisible. The invisibility ends as soon as you attack, cast a spell, or are in bright light.

name: Opportunist
desc: If someone other than you hits a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee attack against that creature.

name: Discipline: Elemental Attunement
desc: No ki cost. As an action, you briefly command the elements nearby to do one of these: make a harmless, instantaneous sensory effect of air, earth, fire or water (a spray of sparks, a puff of breeze, a fine mist, a low rumble of stone); instantly light or put out a candle, torch or small campfire; chill or warm up to 1 pound of nonliving material for up to 1 hour; or make earth, fire, water or mist that fits in a 1-foot cube hold a crude shape you choose for 1 minute.

name: Disciple of the Elements
desc: You learn elemental disciplines, techniques powered by ki. Every monk of this tradition knows Elemental Attunement; pick one other discipline here. You learn one more discipline at 6th, 11th and 17th level, and whenever you learn one you may also swap a discipline you know for another. Disciplines that copy a spell use that spell's casting time and normal rules but need no material components, and any saving throw uses your ki save DC (8 + proficiency bonus + Wisdom modifier). If such a spell gets stronger when cast at a higher level, you can spend extra ki to raise its level by one per extra ki point. The most ki you can spend on one discipline, base cost included, depends on your monk level: 2 at 3rd-4th, 3 at 5th-8th, 4 at 9th-12th, 5 at 13th-16th, and 6 at 17th-20th.

name: Discipline: Breath of Winter
desc: Spend 6 ki points to cast cone of cold: each creature in a 60-foot cone from you makes a Constitution save, taking 8d8 cold damage on a failure or half on a success. A creature it kills is left a frozen statue.

name: Discipline: Clench of the North Wind
desc: Spend 3 ki points to cast hold person: a humanoid you can see within 60 feet makes a Wisdom save or is paralyzed for up to 1 minute (concentration), repeating the save at the end of each of its turns. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one and adds a target.

name: Discipline: Eternal Mountain Defense
desc: Spend 5 ki points to cast stoneskin on yourself: you have resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage for up to 1 hour (concentration).

name: Discipline: Fangs of the Fire Snake
desc: When you take the Attack action on your turn, spend 1 ki point to wreathe your fists and feet in lashing flame: for that action and the rest of the turn your unarmed strikes gain 10 feet of reach and deal fire damage instead of bludgeoning. When one of these strikes hits, you can spend 1 more ki point to add 1d10 fire damage.

name: Discipline: Fist of Four Thunders
desc: Spend 2 ki points to cast thunderwave: each creature in a 15-foot cube starting from you makes a Constitution save, taking 2d8 thunder damage and being pushed 10 feet away on a failure, or half damage and no push on a success. Unsecured objects in the area are pushed too, and the boom is audible 300 feet away. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d8 damage.

name: Discipline: Fist of Unbroken Air
desc: As an action, spend 2 ki points and pick a creature within 30 feet of you. It makes a Strength save. On a failure it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage, plus 1d10 for each extra ki point you spend (up to your maximum), and you can push it up to 20 feet away from you and knock it prone. On a success it takes half damage and is neither pushed nor knocked prone.

name: Discipline: Flames of the Phoenix
desc: Spend 4 ki points to cast fireball: a 20-foot-radius burst at a point you choose within 150 feet. Each creature in it makes a Dexterity save, taking 8d6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and unattended flammable objects catch fire. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d6 damage.

name: Discipline: Gong of the Summit
desc: Spend 3 ki points to cast shatter: a ringing blast fills a 10-foot-radius sphere at a point within 60 feet. Each creature in it makes a Constitution save, taking 3d8 thunder damage on a failure or half on a success; creatures of stone, crystal or metal save with disadvantage, and unattended nonmagical objects there take the damage too. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d8 damage.

name: Discipline: Mist Stance
desc: Spend 4 ki points to cast gaseous form on yourself: for up to 1 hour (concentration) you become a drifting cloud with a 10-foot flying speed. You can slip through tiny cracks and enter other creatures' spaces, have resistance to nonmagical damage and advantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saves, but you can't talk, handle objects, attack or cast spells.

name: Discipline: Ride the Wind
desc: Spend 4 ki points to cast fly on yourself: you gain a flying speed of 60 feet for up to 10 minutes (concentration). If it ends while you are aloft, you fall.

name: Discipline: River of Hungry Flame
desc: Spend 5 ki points to cast wall of fire: an opaque wall of flame within 120 feet, either straight (up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high, 1 foot thick) or a ring (up to 20 feet across, 20 feet high), lasting up to 1 minute (concentration). Creatures in its space when it appears make a Dexterity save, taking 5d8 fire damage or half on a success. One side of your choice burns: a creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side or inside the wall takes 5d8 fire damage, as does a creature entering the wall for the first time on a turn. An extra ki point (if your maximum allows) raises the spell level for +1d8 damage.

name: Discipline: Rush of the Gale Spirits
desc: Spend 2 ki points to cast gust of wind: a line of strong wind 60 feet long and 10 feet wide blasts from you for up to 1 minute (concentration). A creature that starts its turn in the line makes a Strength save or is pushed 15 feet away from you along it, and moving toward you through it costs double movement. It scatters gas and fog and snuffs out candles, torches and other unprotected flames. As a bonus action on later turns you can change the line's direction.

name: Discipline: Shape the Flowing River
desc: As an action, spend 1 ki point and choose an area of water or ice no more than 30 feet on a side within 120 feet of you. You can turn water into ice and ice into water there, and reshape the ice as you like: raise or lower it, dig or fill a trench, raise or flatten a wall, or form a pillar. No change can exceed half the area's largest dimension (a 30-foot square allows up to 15 feet of height or depth). You can't use it to trap or harm a creature in the area.

name: Discipline: Sweeping Cinder Strike
desc: Spend 2 ki points to cast burning hands: each creature in a 15-foot cone from you makes a Dexterity save, taking 3d6 fire damage on a failure or half on a success, and unattended flammable objects in the cone catch fire. Each extra ki point (up to your maximum) raises the spell level by one for +1d6 damage.

name: Discipline: Water Whip
desc: As a bonus action, spend 2 ki points to lash a creature you can see within 30 feet with a whip of water. It makes a Dexterity save. On a failure it takes 3d10 bludgeoning damage, plus 1d10 for each extra ki point you spend (up to your maximum), and you either knock it prone or pull it up to 25 feet toward you. On a success it takes half damage and is neither pulled nor knocked prone.

name: Discipline: Wave of Rolling Earth
desc: Spend 6 ki points to cast wall of stone: a nonmagical stone wall rises at a point within 120 feet, built from up to ten connected 10-by-10-foot panels 6 inches thick (or 10-by-20-foot panels 3 inches thick), lasting up to 10 minutes (concentration) and becoming permanent if you concentrate for the full duration. Each panel has AC 15 and 30 hit points per inch of thickness. A creature caught where the wall forms is pushed to one side (your choice), and if it would be enclosed it can make a Dexterity save to escape first.

name: Elemental Discipline
desc: You learn one more elemental discipline, and you may swap one you already know for another. You can now spend up to 3 ki points on a single discipline (4 from 9th level).

name: Elemental Discipline
desc: You learn one more elemental discipline, and you may swap one you already know for another. You can now spend up to 4 ki points on a single discipline (5 from 13th level).

name: Elemental Discipline
desc: You learn one more elemental discipline, and you may swap one you already know for another. You can now spend up to 6 ki points on a single discipline.

name: Tenets of the Ancients
desc: Kindle the Light: spread hope through mercy, kindness and forgiveness. Shelter the Light: stand guard over goodness, beauty, love and laughter, and over every place where life flourishes. Preserve Your Own Light: keep your own joy alive through song, art and delight, or you will have none left to share. Be the Light: let your courage and gladness be a beacon to everyone lost in despair.

name: Channel Divinity: Nature's Wrath
desc: As an action, spend your Channel Divinity to make spectral vines lunge at a creature you can see within 10 feet of you. It makes a Strength or Dexterity save (its choice) against your spell save DC or is restrained. While restrained, it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns; on a success it breaks free and the vines vanish.

name: Channel Divinity: Turn the Faithless
desc: As an action, present your holy symbol and spend your Channel Divinity. Each fey and fiend within 30 feet of you that can hear you makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC. On a failure it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage: it must spend its turns moving as far from you as it can, can't willingly move within 30 feet of you, can't take reactions, and for its action can only Dash or try to escape something stopping it from moving (or Dodge if it has nowhere to go). While turned, a creature hiding its true form behind an illusion, shapechange or similar effect is revealed.

name: Aura of Warding
desc: You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you take half damage from spells (resistance to spell damage). From 18th level the aura extends to 30 feet.

name: Undying Sentinel
desc: Once per long rest, if something would drop you to 0 hit points without killing you outright, you can stay standing at 1 hit point instead. In addition, old age no longer weakens you, and magic can't age you.

name: Elder Champion
desc: As an action, take on the form of an ancient force of nature (you choose its look) for 1 minute. While transformed: you regain 10 hit points at the start of each of your turns; you can cast a paladin spell with a casting time of 1 action as a bonus action instead; and enemy creatures within 10 feet of you have disadvantage on saving throws against your paladin spells and Channel Divinity options. Once used, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Tenets of Vengeance
desc: Fight the Greater Evil: when you must choose, go after the worse evil rather than the lesser one. No Mercy for the Wicked: ordinary foes may earn your mercy, but your sworn enemies never do. By Any Means Necessary: don't let your scruples stop you from destroying your foes. Restitution: when your foes ruin lives, you share the blame for not stopping them, so you help the people they have harmed.

name: Channel Divinity: Abjure Enemy
desc: As an action, present your holy symbol and spend your Channel Divinity to denounce one creature you can see within 60 feet. Unless it is immune to being frightened, it makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC (fiends and undead have disadvantage). On a failure it is frightened for 1 minute or until it takes any damage, and while frightened its speed is 0 and can't be increased. On a success its speed is halved for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

name: Channel Divinity: Vow of Enmity
desc: Use a bonus action and your Channel Divinity to swear vengeance on a creature you can see within 10 feet. For 1 minute, or until it drops to 0 hit points or falls unconscious, your attack rolls against it have advantage.

name: Relentless Avenger
desc: Landing an opportunity attack lets you give chase: as part of that same reaction, you can move up to half your speed right away, and this movement provokes no opportunity attacks.

name: Soul of Vengeance
desc: Whenever the target of your Vow of Enmity makes an attack, you can answer with your reaction: one melee weapon attack against it, if it is within your reach.

name: Avenging Angel
desc: As an action, transform for 1 hour: wings grow from your back, giving you a flying speed of 60 feet, and you radiate a menacing aura in a 30-foot radius. The first time an enemy enters the aura or starts its turn in it during a battle, it makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or is frightened of you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. Attack rolls against a creature frightened this way have advantage. Once used, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Ranger's Companion
desc: You gain a beast companion: a beast no larger than Medium with a challenge rating of 1/4 or lower. Your proficiency bonus is added to its AC, attack rolls and damage rolls, and to any saves and skills it is proficient in. Its hit point maximum is the higher of its normal maximum and four times your ranger level, and like any creature it can spend Hit Dice during a short rest. It shares your initiative count and only takes an action when you command one. On your turn you can tell it where to move (no action needed), and you can use your action to command it to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge or Help action; once you have Extra Attack, you can also make one weapon attack yourself when you command it to Attack. It uses its reaction (an opportunity attack, say) without waiting for your command. When you are incapacitated or not around, it decides for itself, putting your safety and its own first. When only the two of you are crossing your favored terrain, you can travel stealthily at a normal pace. If it dies, you can bond with a new beast (the same kind or another) that isn't hostile to you by spending 8 hours bonding with it magically.

name: Companion Beast
desc: Choose your animal companion. The numbers below are the beast's ordinary stat block: add your proficiency bonus to its AC, attack rolls and damage rolls, and its hit point maximum is the higher of the listed value and four times your ranger level. With the DM's agreement you can pick another beast of Medium size or smaller and CR 1/4 or lower.

name: Companion: Wolf
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 13, 11 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft. Bite: +4 to hit, 2d4 + 2 piercing, and a creature it hits makes a DC 11 Strength save or is knocked prone. Keen hearing and smell (advantage on Perception that relies on them); Pack Tactics (advantage on attacks when an ally of the wolf is within 5 feet of the target). Perception +3, Stealth +4.

name: Companion: Panther
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 12, 13 HP (3d8), speed 50 ft, climb 40 ft. Bite: +4 to hit, 1d6 + 2 piercing. Claw: +4 to hit, 1d4 + 2 slashing. Pounce: if it moves at least 20 feet straight at a creature and then hits with a claw that turn, the target makes a DC 12 Strength save or is knocked prone, and the panther can bite a prone target as a bonus action. Keen smell. Perception +4, Stealth +6.

name: Companion: Mastiff
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/8. AC 12, 5 HP (1d8), speed 40 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing, and a creature it hits makes a DC 11 Strength save or is knocked prone. Keen hearing and smell. Perception +3.

name: Companion: Boar
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 11, 11 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft. Tusk: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 slashing. Charge: if it moves at least 20 feet straight at a target and then hits with its tusk that turn, it deals an extra 1d6 slashing and a creature makes a DC 11 Strength save or is knocked prone. Relentless (once per short or long rest): if 7 damage or less would drop it to 0 hit points, it drops to 1 instead.

name: Companion: Giant Badger
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 10, 13 HP (2d8), speed 30 ft, burrow 10 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing. Claws: +3 to hit, 2d4 + 1 slashing. Multiattack (bite and claws) once Bestial Fury lets it use that action. Keen smell, darkvision 30 ft.

name: Companion: Giant Weasel
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/8. AC 13, 9 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft. Bite: +5 to hit, 1d4 + 3 piercing. Keen hearing and smell, darkvision 60 ft. Perception +3, Stealth +5.

name: Companion: Giant Wolf Spider
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 13, 11 HP (2d8), speed 40 ft, climb 40 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing, and the target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 2d6 poison damage on a failure or half on a success; if the poison drops it to 0 hit points, it is stable but poisoned and paralyzed for 1 hour. Climbs walls and ceilings freely, senses creatures touching its web, ignores webbing. Blindsight 10 ft, darkvision 60 ft. Perception +3, Stealth +7.

name: Companion: Giant Poisonous Snake
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 14, 11 HP (2d8), speed 30 ft, swim 30 ft. Bite: +6 to hit, reach 10 ft, 1d4 + 4 piercing, and the target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 3d6 poison damage on a failure or half on a success. Blindsight 10 ft. Perception +2.

name: Companion: Giant Crab
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/8. AC 15, 13 HP (3d8), speed 30 ft, swim 30 ft. Claw: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 bludgeoning, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11); it has two claws, each able to grapple one target. Breathes air and water. Blindsight 30 ft. Stealth +4.

name: Companion: Giant Frog
desc: Medium beast, CR 1/4. AC 11, 18 HP (4d8), speed 30 ft, swim 30 ft. Bite: +3 to hit, 1d6 + 1 piercing, and the target is grappled (escape DC 11) and restrained while grappled; the frog can't bite anyone else meanwhile. Swallow (its own action): a bite against a grappled Small or smaller creature swallows it (blinded, restrained, 2d4 acid at the start of each of the frog's turns). Breathes air and water; standing long jump 20 ft, high jump 10 ft. Darkvision 30 ft. Perception +2, Stealth +3.

name: Companion: Flying Snake
desc: Tiny beast, CR 1/8. AC 14, 5 HP (2d4), speed 30 ft, fly 60 ft, swim 30 ft. Bite: +6 to hit, 1 piercing plus 3d4 poison. Flyby (no opportunity attacks when it flies out of reach). Blindsight 10 ft.

name: Companion: Hawk
desc: Tiny beast, CR 0. AC 13, 1 HP (1d4), speed 10 ft, fly 60 ft. Talons: +5 to hit, 1 slashing. Keen sight. Perception +4.

name: Companion: Blood Hawk
desc: Small beast, CR 1/8. AC 12, 7 HP (2d6), speed 10 ft, fly 60 ft. Beak: +4 to hit, 1d4 + 2 piercing. Keen sight; Pack Tactics (advantage on attacks when an ally of the hawk is within 5 feet of the target). Perception +4.

name: Companion: Owl
desc: Tiny beast, CR 0. AC 11, 1 HP (1d4), speed 5 ft, fly 60 ft. Talons: +3 to hit, 1 slashing. Flyby (no opportunity attacks when it flies out of reach); keen hearing and sight. Darkvision 120 ft. Perception +3, Stealth +3.

name: Companion: Giant Rat
desc: Small beast, CR 1/8. AC 12, 7 HP (2d6), speed 30 ft. Bite: +4 to hit, 1d4 + 2 piercing. Keen smell; Pack Tactics (advantage on attacks when an ally of the rat is within 5 feet of the target). Darkvision 60 ft.

name: Exceptional Training
desc: If your companion doesn't attack on one of your turns, you can spend a bonus action to have it Dash, Disengage, Dodge or Help on its turn. Its attacks now count as magical for getting past resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

name: Bestial Fury
desc: Your companion now attacks twice when you command it to take the Attack action (or it can use its Multiattack instead, if it has one).

name: Share Spells
desc: When a spell you cast targets you, you can extend it to your companion as well, provided the beast is within 30 feet of you.

name: Bonus Proficiencies
desc: You become proficient with the disguise kit and the poisoner's kit.

name: Assassinate
desc: You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn yet in the current combat. Every hit you land on a surprised creature is a critical hit.

name: Infiltration Expertise
desc:
By spending 7 days and 25 gp you can set up a dependable false identity: a history, a profession and contacts, backed by fitting clothes, official-looking papers and letters of introduction. It has to be a new persona; you can't take over a real person's identity this way.
Whenever you wear that persona as a disguise, other creatures accept you as that person unless something obviously gives you away.

name: Impostor
desc: After spending at least 3 hours studying a person (listening to them talk, examining their handwriting and watching their mannerisms), you can copy their voice, writing and behaviour flawlessly. Casual observers can't see through it; if a wary creature suspects something is off, you have advantage on Charisma (Deception) checks to keep from being found out.

name: Death Strike
desc: When you hit a surprised creature with an attack, it makes a Constitution saving throw against DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus. On a failure, the damage of that attack against it is doubled.

name: Spellcasting
desc:
You cast spells from the wizard spell list, with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability (spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier; spell attack bonus = your proficiency bonus + your Intelligence modifier). You have 1st-level slots from 3rd level, 2nd-level slots from 7th, 3rd-level from 13th and 4th-level from 19th, and you regain expended slots on a long rest.
Cantrips: you know mage hand plus two other wizard cantrips of your choice, and you learn one more wizard cantrip at 10th level.
Spells known: you start with three 1st-level wizard spells and learn more as you gain levels (your sheet shows how many). They must be enchantment or illusion spells, except for one spell of any school you choose at 3rd level and one more each at 8th, 14th and 20th level.
Whenever you gain a rogue level, you can swap one wizard spell you know for another of a level you have slots for. The new spell must be enchantment or illusion, unless it replaces one of your any-school spells.

name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
desc:
When you cast mage hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and it can do three extra things: slip an object it holds into a container another creature is wearing or carrying, take an object out of such a container, or use thieves' tools at a distance to pick a lock or disarm a trap.
To do one of these without a creature noticing, win a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check against that creature's Wisdom (Perception) check. You can also control the hand with the bonus action from Cunning Action.

name: Magical Ambush
desc: If you are hidden from a creature when you cast a spell on it, that creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the spell this turn.

name: Versatile Trickster
desc: As a bonus action, choose a creature within 5 feet of your mage hand's spectral hand. You have advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

name: Spell Thief
desc:
Right after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area, you can use your reaction to force it to make a saving throw with its spellcasting ability modifier against your spell save DC. On a failure, the spell has no effect on you, and if it is 1st level or higher and of a level you can cast, you steal it: for the next 8 hours you know the spell (even if it isn't a wizard spell) and can cast it with your own spell slots, and the creature can't cast it until those 8 hours are up.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

name: Wild Magic Surge
desc:
Your spells can set off bursts of untamed magic. Once per turn, right after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. On a 1, roll a d100 on the table below and that effect happens. If the effect is a spell, Metamagic can't change it, and it needs no concentration: it simply lasts its full duration.
Wild Magic Surge table (d100):
01-02: For the next minute, roll on this table at the start of each of your turns (ignore this result if it comes up again during that minute).
03-04: For 1 minute, you can see any invisible creature you have line of sight to.
05-06: A modron appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you; the DM picks and controls it, and it vanishes after 1 minute.
07-08: You cast fireball as a 3rd-level spell, centred on yourself.
09-10: You cast magic missile as a 5th-level spell.
11-12: Roll a d10 and change your height by that many inches: shorter on an odd roll, taller on an even roll.
13-14: You cast confusion, centred on yourself.
15-16: For 1 minute, you regain 5 hit points at the start of each of your turns.
17-18: You sprout a long beard of feathers that stays until you sneeze, when the feathers burst off your face.
19-20: You cast grease, centred on yourself.
21-22: If you cast a spell that calls for a saving throw within the next minute, every save against the first such spell is made with disadvantage.
23-24: Your skin turns a vivid blue; a remove curse spell ends this.
25-26: For 1 minute an extra eye opens on your forehead, giving you advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
27-28: For 1 minute, every spell you cast that normally takes 1 action takes 1 bonus action instead.
29-30: You teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
31-32: You are whisked to the Astral Plane until the end of your next turn, then return to the space you left (or the nearest unoccupied space if it is taken).
33-34: The next damaging spell you cast within 1 minute deals maximum damage.
35-36: Roll a d10 and change your age by that many years: younger on an odd roll (never below 1 year old), older on an even roll.
37-38: 1d6 flumphs appear in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you, controlled by the DM and frightened of you; they vanish after 1 minute.
39-40: You regain 2d10 hit points.
41-42: You become a potted plant until the start of your next turn: incapacitated and vulnerable to all damage. If you drop to 0 hit points, the pot breaks and you return to your own form.
43-44: For 1 minute, you can teleport up to 20 feet as a bonus action on each of your turns.
45-46: You cast levitate on yourself.
47-48: A unicorn controlled by the DM appears within 5 feet of you and vanishes after 1 minute.
49-50: For 1 minute you can't speak; pink bubbles drift out of your mouth whenever you try.
51-52: For 1 minute a ghostly shield floats beside you, giving you +2 AC and immunity to magic missile.
53-54: For the next 5d6 days, alcohol can't make you drunk.
55-56: All your hair falls out; it grows back within 24 hours.
57-58: For 1 minute, any flammable object you touch catches fire, unless another creature is wearing or carrying it.
59-60: You regain your lowest-level expended spell slot.
61-62: For 1 minute, you can only speak by shouting.
63-64: You cast fog cloud, centred on yourself.
65-66: Up to three creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you take 4d10 lightning damage.
67-68: You are frightened of the nearest creature until the end of your next turn.
69-70: For 1 minute, every creature within 30 feet of you is invisible; a creature's invisibility ends when it attacks or casts a spell.
71-72: For 1 minute, you have resistance to all damage.
73-74: A random creature within 60 feet of you is poisoned for 1d4 hours.
75-76: For 1 minute you shed bright light in a 30-foot radius; any creature that ends its turn within 5 feet of you is blinded until the end of its next turn.
77-78: You cast polymorph on yourself; if you fail the saving throw, you become a sheep for the spell's duration.
79-80: For 1 minute, illusory butterflies and flower petals drift through the air within 10 feet of you.
81-82: You can take one extra action right away.
83-84: Each creature within 30 feet of you takes 1d10 necrotic damage, and you regain hit points equal to the total necrotic damage dealt.
85-86: You cast mirror image.
87-88: You cast fly on a random creature within 60 feet of you.
89-90: For 1 minute you are invisible and other creatures can't hear you; the invisibility ends if you attack or cast a spell.
91-92: If you die within the next minute, you come straight back to life as if by the reincarnate spell.
93-94: For 1 minute, you are one size category larger.
95-96: For 1 minute, you and every creature within 30 feet of you have vulnerability to piercing damage.
97-98: For 1 minute, faint otherworldly music plays around you.
99-00: You regain all your expended sorcery points.

name: Tides of Chaos
desc: You can give yourself advantage on one attack roll, ability check or saving throw. Once you do, you can't do it again until you finish a long rest. Until then, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table right after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher; if that happens, you get this use back.

name: Bend Luck
desc: When a creature you can see makes an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll a d4 and add it to or subtract it from that roll (your choice). You can do this after the roll but before any of its effects happen.

name: Controlled Chaos
desc: Whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Surge table, you roll twice and choose which of the two results happens.

name: Spell Bombardment
desc: Once per turn, when you roll damage for a spell and one or more dice show their highest possible number, pick one of those dice, roll it again and add the new roll to the damage.

name: Fey Presence
desc:
As an action, you let a flash of fey majesty spill out of you: each creature in a 10-foot cube starting from you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. Every creature that fails is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Misty Escape
desc:
When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You stay invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a spell.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Beguiling Defenses
desc: You can't be charmed. When another creature tries to charm you, you can use your reaction to turn the charm back on it: it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

name: Dark Delirium
desc:
As an action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration breaks (you concentrate as if on a spell); the effect also ends early if the creature takes any damage. While it lasts, the creature believes it is lost in a misty dream-realm whose look you decide, and it can see and hear only itself, you and the illusion.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Awakened Mind
desc: You can speak telepathically to any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don't need a shared language, but the creature has to understand at least one language to follow you.

name: Entropic Ward
desc:
When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to give that roll disadvantage. If the attack misses, you have advantage on your next attack roll against that creature, as long as you make it before the end of your next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Thought Shield
desc: Telepathy and other means can't read your thoughts unless you allow it. You have resistance to psychic damage, and whenever a creature deals psychic damage to you, it takes the same amount of damage that you do.

name: Create Thrall
desc: As an action, you touch an incapacitated humanoid and taint its mind with your patron's alien magic. It is charmed by you until a remove curse spell is cast on it, the charmed condition is removed from it, or you use this feature again. While you and it are on the same plane of existence, you can communicate with it telepathically.

name: Abjuration Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying an abjuration spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Arcane Ward
desc:
When you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher, you can also wrap yourself in a magical ward that lasts until you finish a long rest. You can create the ward only once per long rest.
The ward has a hit point maximum of twice your wizard level + your Intelligence modifier. When you take damage, the ward takes it first; whatever is left after the ward drops to 0 hit points carries over to you. At 0 hit points the ward absorbs nothing, but it still exists, and each time you cast an abjuration spell of 1st level or higher it regains hit points equal to twice the spell's level.

name: Projected Ward
desc: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to have your Arcane Ward absorb that damage instead. If the ward drops to 0 hit points, the creature takes whatever damage is left.

name: Improved Abjuration
desc: When an abjuration spell has you make an ability check as part of casting it (counterspell and dispel magic, for example), you add your proficiency bonus to that check.

name: Spell Resistance
desc: You have advantage on saving throws against spells, and you have resistance to damage from spells.

name: Conjuration Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying a conjuration spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Minor Conjuration
desc: As an action, you create an inanimate, nonmagical object in your hand or in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of you. It must be something you have seen before, no more than 3 feet on a side and no heavier than 10 pounds. It is obviously magical and sheds dim light within 5 feet. It disappears after 1 hour, when you use this feature again, or as soon as it takes or deals any damage.

name: Benign Transposition
desc:
As an action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, or trade places with a willing Small or Medium creature within that range.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest or cast a conjuration spell of 1st level or higher.

name: Focused Conjuration
desc: Taking damage can't break your concentration on a conjuration spell.

name: Durable Summons
desc: Every creature you summon or create with a conjuration spell has 30 temporary hit points.

name: Divination Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying a divination spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Portent
desc: Each time you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and note the results: these are your foretelling rolls. You can replace an attack roll, saving throw or ability check made by you or by a creature you can see with one of them. You must decide before the roll is made, you can do this only once per turn, and each foretelling roll can be used only once. Any you haven't used are lost when you finish your next long rest.

name: Expert Divination
desc: When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher using a spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The regained slot must be of a lower level than the spell you cast, and no higher than 5th level.

name: The Third Eye
desc:
As an action, you sharpen your senses, choosing one of the benefits below each time you use this feature. It lasts until you are incapacitated or you take a short or long rest, and you can't use the feature again until you finish a short or long rest.
Darkvision: you gain darkvision out to 60 feet.
Ethereal Sight: you can see into the Ethereal Plane within 60 feet of you.
Greater Comprehension: you can read any language.
See Invisibility: you can see invisible creatures and objects within 10 feet of you that are in your line of sight.

name: Greater Portent
desc: Your Portent now gives you three foretelling rolls (three d20s) after each long rest instead of two.

name: Enchantment Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying an enchantment spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Hypnotic Gaze
desc:
As an action, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet of you. If it can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn. While charmed this way, its speed is 0 and it is incapacitated and visibly dazed.
On later turns you can spend your action to extend the effect until the end of your next turn. It ends early if you move more than 5 feet away from the creature, if it can neither see nor hear you, or if it takes damage. Once the effect ends, or if the creature succeeds on its first save, you can't use this feature on that creature again until you finish a long rest.

name: Instinctive Charm
desc: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to try to redirect it, as long as another creature is within the attack's range. You decide before you know whether the attack hits. The attacker makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; on a failure it must attack the creature closest to it other than you and itself (the attacker picks if several are equally close). On a success, you can't use this feature on that attacker again until you finish a long rest. Creatures that can't be charmed are immune.

name: Split Enchantment
desc: When you cast an enchantment spell of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature as well.

name: Alter Memories
desc: When you cast an enchantment spell that charms one or more creatures, you can make one of them unaware that it is charmed. In addition, once before the spell ends, you can use your action to blur that creature's memory of the time it spent charmed: it makes an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC or forgets up to 1 + your Charisma modifier hours (minimum 1). You may erase less, and never more than the spell's duration.

name: Illusion Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying an illusion spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Improved Minor Illusion
desc: You learn the minor illusion cantrip (if you already know it, you learn another wizard cantrip of your choice instead), and it doesn't count against your cantrips known. When you cast minor illusion, one casting can create both a sound and an image.

name: Malleable Illusions
desc: While an illusion spell of yours with a duration of 1 minute or longer is active and you can see the illusion, you can use your action to change it, within the spell's normal limits.

name: Illusory Self
desc:
When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to put an illusory double of yourself in the way. The attack automatically misses you, and the double fades.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

name: Illusory Reality
desc: When you cast an illusion spell of 1st level or higher, you can pick one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make it real for 1 minute, using a bonus action on your turn while the spell lasts (an illusory ladder your friends can actually climb, say). The object can't deal damage or directly harm anyone.

name: Necromancy Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying a necromancy spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Grim Harvest
desc: Once per turn, when a spell of 1st level or higher that you cast kills one or more creatures, you regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times its level if it is a necromancy spell. Killing constructs or undead gives you nothing.

name: Undead Thralls
desc:
Animate dead goes into your spellbook if it isn't there already. When you cast it, you can target one extra corpse or pile of bones, raising one more zombie or skeleton.
Every undead you create with a necromancy spell has its hit point maximum increased by your wizard level and adds your proficiency bonus to its weapon damage rolls.

name: Inured to Undeath
desc: You have resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced.

name: Command Undead
desc:
As an action, choose an undead you can see within 60 feet of you. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a success, you can never use this feature on it again. On a failure, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.
Clever undead resist: one with Intelligence 8 or higher has advantage on the save, and one with Intelligence 12 or higher that fails can repeat the save at the end of every hour until it succeeds and breaks free.

name: Transmutation Savant
desc: The gold and time you spend copying a transmutation spell into your spellbook are halved.

name: Minor Alchemy
desc: You can temporarily turn a nonmagical object made entirely of wood, stone (not gemstones), iron, copper or silver into a different one of those materials. Each 10 minutes of work transforms up to 1 cubic foot. The change lasts 1 hour or until your concentration breaks (you concentrate as if on a spell), then the material returns to what it was.

name: Transmuter's Stone
desc:
Over 8 hours you can craft a transmuter's stone. Whoever carries it (you, or someone you give it to) gains one benefit you choose when you make it:
Darkvision out to 60 feet.
+10 feet of speed while unencumbered.
Proficiency in Constitution saving throws.
Resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage (pick the type each time you choose this benefit).
While the stone is on you, you can switch its benefit each time you cast a transmutation spell of 1st level or higher. If you make a new stone, the old one stops working.

name: Shapechanger
desc: Polymorph goes into your spellbook if it isn't there already. You can cast it without using a spell slot, but then it can target only you, and you must become a beast of challenge rating 1 or lower. After casting it this way, you can't do so again until you finish a short or long rest; you can still cast it normally with a slot.

name: Master Transmuter
desc:
As an action, you can release all the magic stored in your transmuter's stone at once for one of the effects below. The stone is destroyed, and you can't make a new one until you finish a long rest.
Major Transformation: after 10 minutes of handling a nonmagical object no bigger than a 5-foot cube, you turn it into another nonmagical object of similar size and mass and of equal or lower value.
Panacea: a creature you touch is cured of all curses, diseases and poisons and regains all its hit points.
Restore Life: you cast raise dead on a creature you touch with the stone, without using a spell slot or needing the spell in your spellbook.
Restore Youth: a willing creature you touch with the stone becomes 3d10 years younger in appearance (minimum 13 years old); its lifespan is not extended.
